theorem actual_fixed_shift_preserves_any_convergent_time_average (u : ℕ → ℝ)
    (K : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hu : Tendsto (fun N => average u N) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    Tendsto (fun N => average (fun n => u (n+K)) N) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  let C : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range K,u n
  have ha := hu.comp (tendsto_add_atTop_nat K)
  have hk : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (K:ℝ)/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using (tendsto_const_nhds (x:=(K:ℝ))).mul (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜:=ℝ))
  have hc : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => C/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using (tendsto_const_nhds (x:=C)).mul (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜:=ℝ))
  have ht : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (1+(K:ℝ)/(N:ℝ))*average u (N+K)-C/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
    convert ((tendsto_const_nhds (x:=(1:ℝ))).add hk).mul ha |>.sub hc using 1 <;> simp
  apply ht.congr'
  filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (1:ℕ)] with N hN
  have hn : (N:ℝ)≠0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : N≠0)
  have hnk : ((N+K:ℕ):ℝ)≠0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : N+K≠0)
  have hs : (∑ n ∈ range (N+K),u n)=C+∑ n ∈ range N,u (n+K) := by
    rw [Nat.add_comm N K,sum_range_add]
    dsimp [C]
    simp_rw [Nat.add_comm K]
  unfold average
  rw [hs]
  push_cast
  field_simp
  ring

theorem actual_arbitrary_fixed_prefix_followed_by_the_same_shifted_tail
    (u v : ℕ → ℝ) (K : ℕ) (h : ∀ n, u (n+K)=v n) (L : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun N => average u N) atTop (𝓝 L) ↔
      Tendsto (fun N => average v N) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  constructor
  · intro hu
    have ht := actual_fixed_shift_preserves_any_convergent_time_average u K L hu
    simpa only [h] using ht
  · intro hv
    let w : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => if n < K then 0 else v (n-K)
    have hwshift : ∀ n, w (n+K)=v n := by intro n; simp [w]
    have hw : Tendsto (fun N => average w N) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
      let C : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ range K,w n
      have hc : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => C/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
        simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using (tendsto_const_nhds (x:=C)).mul (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜:=ℝ))
      have hk : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (K:ℝ)/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
        simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using (tendsto_const_nhds (x:=(K:ℝ))).mul (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜:=ℝ))
      have hn : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => N-K) atTop atTop := tendsto_sub_atTop_nat K
      have ht := hc.add (((tendsto_const_nhds (x:=(1:ℝ))).sub hk).mul (hv.comp hn))
      have : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => C/(N:ℝ)+(1-(K:ℝ)/(N:ℝ))*average v (N-K)) atTop (𝓝 L) := by simpa using ht
      apply this.congr'
      filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop (K+1)] with N hN
      have hle : K≤N := by omega
      have hn0 : (N:ℝ)≠0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : N≠0)
      have hnk : ((N-K:ℕ):ℝ)≠0 := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : N-K≠0)
      have hs : (∑ n ∈ range N,w n)=C+∑ n ∈ range (N-K),v n := by
        calc
          (∑ n ∈ range N,w n) = ∑ n ∈ range (K+(N-K)),w n := by exact congrArg (fun T : ℕ => ∑ n ∈ range T,w n) (by omega : N=K+(N-K))
          _ = C+∑ n ∈ range (N-K),v n := by
            rw [sum_range_add]
            dsimp [C]
            simp_rw [Nat.add_comm K,hwshift]
      unfold average
      rw [hs]
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hle]
      have hnk' : (N:ℝ)-(K:ℝ)≠0 := by simpa only [Nat.cast_sub hle] using hnk
      field_simp [hn0,hnk']
    exact (actual_any_fixed_finite_prefix_change_preserves_time_average_limits u w K
      (fun n hn => by obtain ⟨j,rfl⟩:=Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hn; simpa [w,Nat.add_comm] using h j) L).mpr hw
end SafeLearning.CompleteMonitoringShiftedMean23

def average (u : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ := (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,u n)/(N:ℝ)

private theorem finite_prefix_average_transfer (u v : ℕ → ℝ) (K : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n, K≤n → u n=v n) (L : ℝ)
    (hv : Tendsto (fun N => average v N) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    Tendsto (fun N => average u N) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  let C : ℝ := (∑ n ∈ Finset.range K,u n)-(∑ n ∈ Finset.range K,v n)
  have he : (fun N => average u N-average v N) =ᶠ[atTop] (fun N => C/(N:ℝ)) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop K] with N hN
    have hs : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,u n)-(∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,v n)=C := by
      rw [show N=K+(N-K) by omega,Finset.sum_range_add,Finset.sum_range_add]
      have ht : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N-K),u (K+n))=∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N-K),v (K+n) := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro n hn
        exact h (K+n) (by omega)
      rw [ht]
      dsimp [C]
      ring
    simpa [average,sub_div] using congrArg (fun x : ℝ => x/(N:ℝ)) hs
  have hc : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => C/(N:ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using (tendsto_const_nhds (x:=C)).mul (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜:=ℝ))
  have hd : Tendsto (fun N => average u N-average v N) atTop (𝓝 0) := hc.congr' he.symm
  simpa using hd.add hv

theorem actual_any_fixed_finite_prefix_change_preserves_time_average_limits
    (u v : ℕ → ℝ) (K : ℕ) (h : ∀ n, K≤n → u n=v n) (L : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun N => average u N) atTop (𝓝 L) ↔
      Tendsto (fun N => average v N) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  constructor
  · exact finite_prefix_average_transfer v u K (fun n hn => (h n hn).symm) L
  · exact finite_prefix_average_transfer u v K h L

end SafeLearning.CompleteMonitoringDualTrajectory23

No boundedness of the infinite sequences is needed because the finite prefix contributes a fixed finite real C. N=0 is irrelevant to the eventual argument; the real division convention introduces no asymptotic gap.

cmdp.html::node-1138.source_text: (b) Because the agent must leave $R_0$ at every step, the long-run fractions $(V_0,V_1,V_2)$ of any policy satisfy $V_0\le\tfrac12$, and every such point of the simplex is attained (from $R_0$ pick $R_1$ with probability $q$, stay in $R_i$ with probability $a_i$). The achievable set is thus the quadrilateral with vertices $v_1=(0,1,0)$ (stay in $R_1$), $v_2=(0,0,1)$ (stay in $R_2$), $v_3=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12,0)$ (alternate $R_0,R_1$), $v_4=(\tfrac12,0,\tfrac12)$ (alternate $R_0,R_2$). $L=V_0+\lambda_1V_1+\lambda_2V_2-\tfrac{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}{3}$ is linear in the fractions, so it is maximised on a face; up to the constant $-\tfrac{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}{3}$ its values at the four vertices are $\lambda_1,\ \lambda_2,\ \tfrac{1+\lambda_1}{2},\ \tfrac{1+\lambda_2}{2}$. The optimum $(\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac13)$ is an interior point, so it maximises $L$ only if $L$ is constant on the whole quadrilateral, i.e. $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=1$. For $\lambda_1\gt\lambda_2$ the maximal vertex is $v_1$ (if $\lambda_1\ge1$) or $v_3$ (if $\lambda_1\le1$), and every maximiser has $V_2=0$: infeasible; symmetrically for $\lambda_2\gt\lambda_1$. For $\lambda_1=\lambda_2\lt1$ the maximisers form the edge $v_3$–$v_4$: return to $R_0$ at once, $V_1+V_2=\tfrac12\lt\tfrac23$, infeasible. For $\lambda_1=\lambda_2\gt1$ they form the edge $v_1$–$v_2$, so every maximiser has $V_0=0$. A stationary maximiser enters one region and stays there; it is feasible in expectation when the probability $q$ of entering $R_1$ lies in $[\tfrac13,\tfrac23]$, while each trajectory starves one region. A history-dependent maximiser can do better on feasibility. Staying $n$ steps in $R_1$, then $n$ steps in $R_2$, for $n=1,2,\dots$ (passing through $R_0$ once per block) visits $R_0$ only $O(\sqrt T)$ times in $T$ steps, so it reaches $(0,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ and meets both constraints on its single trajectory. All of them are worthless, though: return $0$ against $P^\star=\tfrac13$. In no case is a Lagrangian maximiser optimal.

cmdp.html::node-1141.source_text: (c) Executing $\pi(\cdot\mid s,\lambda_k)$ with the dual update, the multiplier of a region whose visit deficit is growing rises. Once it exceeds both $1$ and the other multiplier ($\lambda_i\gt\max(1,\lambda_j)$, the vertex $v_i$ of (b)), the maximiser heads for $R_i$ and stays there. While the deficit is repaid the multiplier falls, and once $\lambda_i\lt\max(1,\lambda_j)$ the maximiser leaves $R_i$: for $R_j$ if $\lambda_j\gt1$, otherwise back to $R_0$, alternating with the region of larger multiplier. At ties the Lagrangian does not decide, and the policy's tie-breaking does. The trajectory time-shares between behaviours that are individually infeasible, and its long-run fractions satisfy both constraints (Theorem 1 of Section 7). A fixed-$\lambda$ policy $\pi(a\mid s)$ has to commit to one maximiser of $L(\cdot,\lambda)$ and, by (b), commits to one that is infeasible or has zero return unless $\lambda=(1,1)$, where the Lagrangian gives it no information at all. The multiplier is a sufficient statistic of the constraint history that tells the policy which region is behind schedule; conditioning on it is what makes the switching implementable. (The fair-coin policy is a legitimate stationary Markov policy, so the failure is one of recovery from the Lagrangian, not of representation.)
